IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Tuesday, September 22, 2026**

**LU-494 Milwaukee, WI** is running hot right now. Sixty-four calls, **$60.00/hr** on the top single call (Gurtz Electric's Port Washington Data Center gig), and both Gurtz and Cupertino are stacking 30-man crews each with JW wage plus **$10/hr base wage** incentives baked in. That's real money on a data center build. Book depth is tight—296 hands against 64 calls means you're looking at maybe Book 2 movement if you're third-in.

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** has the volume: 75 calls hunting 584 hands. Miller Electrical, Inglett & Stubbs, and Whitehead Electric are all locked into QTS Fayetteville data center work at **$42/hr**—tray hanging, feeder pulls, real inside wireman work. Scale's fair for the region and the board is soft enough that being first or second book actually matters here.

**LU-575 Portsmouth, OH** is a sniper shot. Only 8 calls, but TSG just posted 95 JW slots on Amazon North Campus Jeffersonville—that single call dwarfs the whole board. Starts Monday, Sept 28, running 4-10s plus an 8 most weeks. Book 1 gets consumed immediately; Book 2 moves fast on something this big.

**LU-545 St. Joseph, MO** is a grind but pays: six calls total, but Enerfab and Newtron are both pulling JWs into Turney Energy Center at **$68.51/hr**—the single highest rate on this board by far. Fifteen slots with Enerfab, six with Newtron. Tight local, tighter book, real industrial money.

**LU-354 Salt Lake City, UT** runs steady data center work—Cache Valley, Skyline, Wasatch, and Rydalch all staffing META, QTS, and P&G jobs at **$46.22/hr** across the board, with per diem hitting **$225/day** on 10-hour days and OT kickers on weekends.

**LU-917 Meridian, MS** is a sleeper: only 4 calls on the board but Rosendin Electric just dropped 45 JW slots for Compass Data Center nightshift work with **$10 above scale** per diem incentive and a 17.3% shift differential. Book 1 vanishes in hours.

Data centers are eating wiremen. Amazon, QTS, Compass, META—they're the gravity well right now, and the locals nearest those projects are moving bodies fast.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Tuesday, September 22, 2026**

**LU-84 Newnan, GA** is running hot with 17 calls chasing 95 hands. SERVICE ELECTRIC is stacking **$56.80/hr** work on two separate Journeyman Lineman calls out of Social Circle—both energized GTC work requiring Quanta barehand cert. That's the board's ceiling. HEART UTILITIES has 20 JLs moving to Savannah at **$46.80/hr** with **$150/day per diem** on a 5-10 schedule. Real volume here.

**LU-175 Chattanooga, TN** sits at 15 calls, 52 hands deep, but this is nuclear and locked-down work. Day and Zimmermann's Watts Bar MODS call (7 Inside JWs) and Energy Solutions/Williams on the TVA nuclear plants both require TVA clearance—that's your gate. NABCO's Chickamauga Dam Lock project is the outlier, worth exploring if you don't have the nuclear credentials yet.

**LU-429 Nashville, TN** has just 5 calls but NEWTRON is pushing 25 Inside JWs to Google in Clarksville on nights, 7-12s. That's real data-center velocity. Smaller plays from SERVICE ELECTRIC and J & H on Cumberland City combined cycle round out what looks like a tightening board.

**LU-1547 Anchorage, AK** is anomaly central: 25 calls chasing only 29 hands means book depth is nearly gone. New Horizons Telecom and Alaska Communications are running low-wage fill (cell tower tech at **$24.18/hr**, remediation at **$25/hr**), but Golden Valley EI&C and Valley Electric's Juneau wireman work offer real traction if you're certified and mobile enough for Alaska winters.

**LU-291 Boise, ID** is Micron-heavy: Rosendin and Prime Controls both running Inside JWs at **$45.33/hr base** plus **$20/hr incentive** on the OPAL and ID1 builds. Travel pay hits **$200/day worked** at Rosendin. PLA jobs, 5/8s and 60/60/5 schedules—solid long-term moves if you can lock in.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** is a data-center sprint: Parsons Electric's 15 Inside JWs at the Polaris Forge in Harwood, **$44.80/hr**, **$100/day base per diem** (non-taxed), **$150/day weekends**, plus **$100/day ND license incentive**, running 6-10s. That's real per-diem architecture and the incentives stack.

Data-center work and nuclear clearance jobs are moving the boards right now; residential and transmission rebuilds lag.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Tuesday, September 22, 2026**

**LU-208 Denver, CO** is running hot with 9 calls and 26 hands needed—your best volume play in today's board. US Eng. Metalworks is staffing a shop run with 3 SS fitters and 4 SS TIG welders. Trautman and Shreve's got fab work with combo welders split day and swing. The standout: Tolin Mountains out of Vail, Aspen, and Summit County is running multiple fitter jobs on 4/10s with some OT, and they're covering lodging with per diem—that's your lifestyle call if you want elevation and steady hours.

**LU-776 Lima, OH** sits at 5 calls, 40 hands—smaller board but solid contractors. Gem's Fab Shop is looking for combo welders on 6-10s (testing required). Graham's Cenovus Maintenance gig runs pipefitters 6-10s starting at 6am with spotty OT. Nooter has another Cenovus Fab shop slot for pipefitters on 7-10s with **$125/day** PD incentive pay. All three major calls want currency updates, so verify your card before you move.

**LU-213 St John, NB** is thin—just 1 call—but it's fat: CAM's Irving Oil Refinery shutdown needs F3/F4 and F6/F5 certified welders on 4x10s-plus with shutdown incentives. This is a test-in gig for refinery work, not a casual book. If you've got your certs current, this one's worth the border crossing.

**LU-208 Construction** (nested under Denver) has 3 hands needed for Broadcom in Fort Collins—high purity tube-bending fitters only. Specialty work, specialty rate.

The story: Denver's scale and volume are pulling hands mountain-west; Lima's maintenance work is stable but commodity; St John's refinery shutdown is a hard skill gate. Specialty fab and refinery certifications are moving the needle.
